Abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13617.title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13617.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13617v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_\chi/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_\chi\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_\chi\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13655.title: Toward Pseudorange-Based PNT with Starlink: A Mock Fused LEO GNSS Implementation
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13655.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13655v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present experimental results from Starlink for pseudorange-based positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT), emulating a system that fuses a primary communications mission with a secondary low-Earth orbit (LEO) PNT mission. Legacy global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations faceinherent vulnerabilities and signal limitations, prompting growing interest in
  broadband LEO constellations---such as SpaceX's Starlink---for resilient PNT. However, opportunistic use of stand-alone Starlink signals fails to achieve
  GNSS-competitive accuracy due to frame timing irregularities and reliance on uncorrected poor-quality publicly available ephemeris data. To overcome these limitations, we present a mock
  implementation of a fused LEO GNSS architecture. Our method extracts time-of-arrival observables from live Starlink Ku-band downlinks and pairs them with high-fidelity, beam-specific orbit and clock models distributed as if provided natively by the constellation operator. In a field campaign, and despite constraints imposed by consumer-grade receiver hardware, the method
  yields 95% error bounds of 2.33 m horizontally (semi-major axis), 3.37 m vertically, and 11.19 ns in timing, with the actual solution errors falling well within these bounds.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.13842.title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Through Exponential Production Mechanism
arxiv.org/abs/2611.13842.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.13842v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Exponential production of dark matter has been introduced recently as one of the alternatives to the widely studied thermal production of dark matter scenarios. This non-thermal production mechanism leads to the exponential growth in the abundance of the dark matter ($\chi$) through its scatterings with the bath particle ($\xi$), viz. $\chi + \xi \to \chi + \chi$. In our framework, we consider a scalar dark matter $\chi$ charged under $Z_3$ symmetry and bath particle $\xi$ to be standard model singlet and determine the maximum mass of the dark matter using the criteria of perturbativity. We find that dark matter has an upper mass around the ballpark of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15})$ GeV for the cases when the bath particle mass is similar to the dark matter mass. The computations are largely performed with minimal model dependence and will hold in any scenario where the renormalizable couplings driving the exponential growth effectively reduce to $\chi^3\xi$ interactions. Thus, in exponential production of dark matter, we have a possibility of an ultra-heavy dark matter with large couplings, making the scenario phenomenologically interesting. Later, we extend the simplified dark matter model to a UV-complete Dirac Type-I seesaw model where the $Z_3$ symmetry is obtained as a residual unbroken subgroup of a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, providing a natural connection with the neutrino sector.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14077.title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14077.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14077v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14151.title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14151.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14151v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14197.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14197.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14197v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14306.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14306.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14306v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.14331.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
arxiv.org/abs/2611.14331.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.14331v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

arxiv.org/abs/2503.14741.title: Validation of the DESI DR2 Ly$\alpha$ BAO analysis using synthetic datasets
arxiv.org/abs/2503.14741.excerpt:
arXiv:2503.14741v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The second data release (DR2) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), containing data from the first three years of observations, doubles the number of Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest spectra in DR1 and it provides the largest dataset of its kind. To ensure a robust validation of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) analysis using Ly$\alpha$ forests, we have made significant updates compared to DR1 to both the mocks and the analysis framework used in the validation. In particular, we present CoLoRe-QL, a new set of Ly$\alpha$ mocks that use a quasi-linear input power spectrum to incorporate the non-linear broadening of the BAO peak. We have also increased the number of realisations used in the validation to 400, compared to the 150 realisations used in DR1. Finally, we present a detailed study of the impact of quasar redshift errors on the BAO measurement, and we compare different strategies to mask Damped Lyman-$\alpha$ Absorbers (DLAs) in our spectra. The BAO measurement from the Ly$\alpha$ dataset of DESI DR2 is presented in a companion publication.

arxiv.org/abs/2504.13705.title: Interpretation of fast radio bursts from CHIME/FRB baseband data
arxiv.org/abs/2504.13705.excerpt:
arXiv:2504.13705v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are radio pulses that originate from cosmological distances. Thousands of FRB sources have been discovered, but their origins remain unknown. Analyses of the energy function and redshift evolution of the volumetric event rate could provide crucial insights into FRB progenitors. In this paper, we used the $V_\mathrm{max}$ method to analyse the FRB energy functions and volumetric event rate evolution based on CHIME/FRB BaseCat 1 data. The baseband data provide improved fluence and bandwidth measurements compared to Catalogue 1, enabling a more robust analysis of FRB energy and population studies. The $V_\mathrm{max}$ method allows us to investigate volumetric event rate evolution as a function of redshift without any prior assumptions. The selection functions for baseband data were derived to re-weight the samples when calculating the number density. We observe Schechter-like shapes for the energy function with a unified slope index of $\gamma \in [-1.8, -1.6]$. Neither the cosmic star formation rate density (SFRD) nor the cosmic stellar-mass density scenario can be ruled out. We further discuss the scenario that FRBs are primarily produced from systems that evolve with a delay relative to SFRD. The rate evolution trend suggests a scenario of a delayed model with a delay time $\tau \approx 4.66$ Gyr, hinting at delayed core-collapse supernovae or compact binary mergers. Our work highlights the importance of baseband data, and the BaseCat 2 data are required to explore FRB populations and rate evolution.

arxiv.org/abs/2506.01786.title: Science Prospects for the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory: SWGO
arxiv.org/abs/2506.01786.excerpt:
arXiv:2506.01786v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Ground-based gamma-ray astronomy is now well established as a key observational approach to address critical topics at the frontiers of astroparticle physics and high-energy astrophysics. Whilst the field of TeV astronomy was once dominated by arrays of atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes, ground-level particle detection has now been demonstrated to be an equally viable and strongly complementary approach. Ground-level particle detection provides continuous monitoring of the overhead sky, critical for the mapping of extended structures and capturing transient phenomena. As demonstrated by HAWC and LHAASO, the technique provides the best available sensitivity above a few tens of TeV, and for the first time access to the PeV energy range. Despite the success of this approach, there is so far no major ground-level particle-based observatory with access to the Southern sky. HESS, located in Namibia, is the only major gamma-ray instrument in the Southern Hemisphere, and has shown the extraordinary richness of the inner galaxy in the TeV band, but is limited in terms of field of view and energy reach.
  SWGO is an international effort to construct the first wide-field instrument in the south with deep sensitivity from 100s of GeV into the PeV domain. The project is now close to the end of its development phase and planning for construction of the array in Chile has begun. Here we describe the baseline design, expected sensitivity and resolution, and describe in detail the main scientific topics that will be addressed by this new facility and its initial phase SWGO-A. We show that SWGO will have a transformational impact on a wide range of topics from cosmic-ray acceleration and transport to the nature of dark matter. SWGO represents a key piece of infrastructure for multi-messenger astronomy in the next decade, with strong scientific synergies with the nearby CTA Observatory.

arxiv.org/abs/2510.02432.title: The Entangling of Supernova Feedback Impacts with Coarsening Simulation Resolution
arxiv.org/abs/2510.02432.excerpt:
arXiv:2510.02432v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: It is often understood that supernova (SN) feedback in galaxies is responsible for regulating star formation (SF) and generating gaseous outflows. However, a detailed look at the small-scale effects of SNe on the interstellar medium (ISM) in simulations shows that the macroscopic processes of SF suppression and outflow generation proceed in distinct channels. We demonstrate this finding in two independent simulations of isolated dwarf galaxies with very high (m_gas ~ Msun) numerical resolution, LYRA and RIGEL. Our findings suggest that the macroscopic effect of a given SN on the galaxy is best predicted by its local density. Outflows are primarily linked to SNe in diffuse regions expanding to their cooling radii on large (~kpc) scales, while dense SF regions are disrupted in a localized (~pc) manner. However, these separate feedback channels are only distinguishable at very high resolutions capable of following mass scales \lesssim 10^2 \msun. When averaging on coarser scales, ISM densities are greatly mis-estimated, and variations between different SF and SNe-affected regions are severely washed out. It therefore cannot be __self-consistently__ determined, from coarse-resolution information __alone__, (1) whether a SN tends to contribute to outflows or direct SF suppression, and (2) the rate of SF in a given region. In particular, commonly used parameters in coarse-resolution (subgrid) models, such as the SN cooling radius and SF density threshold, may require more detailed treatments informed by high-resolution studies.

arxiv.org/abs/2510.11156.title: Measuring the Evolution of Bulge, Disk and Colour Gradients in HST Observations of Galaxies with 3D Modelling
arxiv.org/abs/2510.11156.excerpt:
arXiv:2510.11156v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We measure galaxy structural properties and colour gradients using HST images to trace the evolution of galaxy components. We develop and apply a physically motivated 3D bulge+disk modelling framework, jointly fitting the components in 2505 galaxies in GOODS-South across seven bands (bvizYJH) to $I_{\rm AB}=25.5$, accounting for different component ellipticities and inclination-dependent dust extinction. Extinction strongly affects structural parameters and colour gradients in $\sim$26% of the sample - primarily edge-on galaxies with central obscuration (B-band face-on optical depth $\tau \simeq 4$) that reveal clear bulge components in the near-infrared. Despite irregular morphologies, the model captures observed colour gradients well. Bulges at $z \sim 1$ differ markedly from $z \sim 0$, with typical S\'ersic index $n \sim 1.0$ and bulge-to-disc size ratio $R_{\rm e}/h_{\rm d} \sim 0.15$, suggesting most galaxies host pseudo-bulges formed via secular evolution. Galaxy ellipticity correlates strongly with disk scale-length. We trace bulge and disk evolution from $z \sim 0$ to $z \sim 2.5$: bulges are redder than disks (observed-frame) at $z < 1.4$, but colours converge at higher redshifts and fainter magnitudes. Redder galaxies show redder cores relative to their outskirts, and brighter galaxies have redder cores. These results provide new measurements of bulge and disk structural properties at $z \sim 1$ and observational constraints on their evolution, while also providing empirically motivated input distributions for assessing colour gradient systematics in weak lensing surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2512.03411.title: Conformal Holographic Dark Energy and the Neutrino-Mass Tension
arxiv.org/abs/2512.03411.excerpt:
arXiv:2512.03411v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent DESI results suggest a preference for evolving dark energy (DE) over a cosmological constant, motivating the exploration of alternative models for the background expansion. These data also lead to neutrino-mass constraints close to the lower bounds permitted by oscillation experiments. In this work, we propose and test a conformal holographic dark energy (CHDE) model in which the DE density depends on a power law of the conformal time, characterized by an exponent $n$. The model introduces one additional parameter relative to $\Lambda$CDM and reduces to it in the limit $n=0$. We confront CHDE with BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia datasets, following the combinations used by DESI, and perform parameter inference in both flat and non-flat cosmologies. We find a consistent preference for $n\simeq -0.25$ to $-0.32$, with uncertainties below $\pm 0.1$, and disfavor the $\Lambda$CDM limit at the $4.4$--$4.5\sigma$ level; however, the model-comparison statistics provide no consistent preference for CHDE over $\Lambda$CDM. The resulting neutrino-mass constraints remain compatible with terrestrial limits and yield posterior distributions that peak at positive values, avoiding the negative-mass preference found in $\Lambda$CDM. The CHDE model is therefore consistent with current observational constraints and provides a viable alternative to constant dark energy.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.13385.title: Modeling Globular Cluster Stellar Streams with a Basis-Expansion N-body Code
arxiv.org/abs/2602.13385.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.13385v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Globular cluster stellar streams probe galaxy-formation processes and can potentially reveal the distribution of dark matter in galaxies. In many theoretical studies, streams are modeled with particle-spray or direct N-body codes. But particle-spray methods abstract away the internal dynamics of the progenitor by making strong assumptions about the escape physics, while direct N-body is prohibitively expensive for realistic (N>10^5) systems. In this paper, we present the stream-modeling capabilities of KRIOS, a new basis-expansion N-body code for collisional stellar dynamics, that bridges this runtime vs. accuracy gap. We show that KRIOS reproduces NBODY6++GPU cluster models, and their associated streams, more accurately than particle spray in a fraction of the NBODY6++GPU wall-clock time. We then compare KRIOS to various particle-spray methods on 10 orbits similar to known Milky Way streams. The morphology and kinematics of these streams most disagree when the progenitor is tightly bound to the host, as these systems are often subject to stronger tidal forces. Finally, we discuss which elements of the progenitor physics are most important for modeling stellar streams and how these might be incorporated into particle-spray methods.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.28862.title: Enhanced Multiphase Circumgalactic Medium and Gas Cycling in Galaxy Mergers
arxiv.org/abs/2603.28862.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.28862v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate the impact of galaxy mergers on the circumgalactic medium (CGM) using the FIREbox cosmological hydrodynamic simulation. By comparing matched samples of merging and isolated galaxies with stellar masses $M_\star \sim 10^{10}$--$10^{11} \, \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ at $z=0$ and merger mass ratios larger than $1:10$, we find that mergers significantly alter CGM properties. Merging systems exhibit enhanced radiative cooling, leading to shorter cooling times than free-fall times across large CGM volumes. This results in amplified multiphase structure and increased cool/cold gas content ($T \sim 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$) compared to isolated galaxies. Both inflow and outflow mass fluxes are elevated across a wide range, and the enhancement is mostly pronounced in cool ($\sim10^4\mathrm{K}$) and hot ($\sim10^6\mathrm{K}$) phases by at least $\sim$1 dex in mergers, with cool gas primarily generated in-situ via radiative cooling rather than from pre-existing streams. Gas cycling analysis reveals that mergers fundamentally accelerate CGM processing, amplifying the effective transfer rate from cold/cool cosmic inflow to galaxy inflow by factors of $\sim 27$ through rapid cycling of inflowing gas through intermediate CGM phases, efficiently fueling the ISM and star formation. The enhanced cool gas content in mergers produces elevated column densities for low- and intermediate-temperature ion species in the inner CGM, while high-temperature species remain largely unaffected.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.01420.title: Low-mass failed supernovae and the $10\,M_{\odot}$ peak in the merging black hole mass distribution
arxiv.org/abs/2604.01420.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.01420v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave observations reveal that the rate of merging black holes drops by $\sim2$ orders of magnitude from component masses $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ to $\sim 15\,M_{\odot}$. The increased compactness of the black hole progenitor cores may contribute to the $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ overdensity, but cannot fully explain the rate difference. In this paper, we consider the possibility that the overdensity is reinforced by supernova processes that result in efficient black hole formation from direct collapse in a narrow range around $10\, M_{\odot}$. We extend previous studies by considering a distinct subpopulation of failed-supernovae black holes, possibly separated by a gap in the primary mass distribution from the rest of the population. Using 153 observations from the latest GWTC-4.0 catalog, we confirm a strong peak in the primary mass distribution at $10\,M_{\odot}$, with a peak rate density of $7.36_{-3.11}^{+6.35}$ $M_{\odot}^{-1}\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}$. The rate drops sharply and becomes consistent with zero at the 90 % level for primary mass $m_1\in (12.0, 16.1)\, M_{\odot}$, then rises again to confidently nonzero values above $\sim 16\,M_{\odot}$ before falling at higher masses. Our results reveal structure in the mass distribution in the $10-20\,M_{\odot}$ range, with rate changes of multiple orders of magnitude across a few solar masses, consistent with a distinct population of failed-supernova black holes. These conclusions persist in the latest GWTC-5.0 catalog.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.19830.title: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) Antarctic Balloon Payload
arxiv.org/abs/2604.19830.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.19830v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The General Antiparticle Spectrometer (GAPS) is an Antarctic stratospheric balloon mission designed to provide unmatched sensitivity to low-energy (< 0.25 GeV/n) cosmic-ray antiprotons, antideuterons, and antihelium nuclei as signatures of dark matter. The distinctive GAPS particle identification technique relies on measuring the energy loss along the track of an incoming antinucleus as it slows down and is captured into an exotic atom, and then detecting the de-excitation X-rays and the nuclear annihilation products. This measurement is realized using a Tracker composed of more than 1000 custom silicon strip detectors and a plastic scintillator time-of-flight (TOF) system instrumenting more than 40 m$^2$. Together, these subsystems provide the velocity and energy resolution, stopping power, particle tracking, and X-ray identification necessary to distinguish rare antinucleus signals from the abundant positive-nucleus backgrounds, all within the constraints of a high-altitude mission. A multi-loop capillary heat pipe system has been developed to maintain the tracker operating temperature with significant mass and power savings over a conventional pump-based system. The first GAPS science payload flew for 25 days during the 2025/26 NASA Antarctic balloon campaign. We detail the design, integration, and commissioning of the payload prior to flight.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.22401.title: Quiescent fractions in high-redshift galaxy groups reflect their hot-or-cold state of gas accretion
arxiv.org/abs/2604.22401.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.22401v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Cold accretion and quenching are closely related aspects of galaxy evolution, as sustained gas supply is required to maintain star formation. High-redshift galaxy groups therefore provide a valuable laboratory for testing how the thermal state of accreting gas relates to the emergence of quiescence. We measure quiescent fractions in a sample of 16 spectroscopically confirmed galaxy groups at $1.6<3.6$, spanning halo masses from $10^{12.8},{\rm M_\odot}$ to $10^{13.9},{\rm M_\odot}$, by fitting the SEDs of candidate member galaxies selected from the COSMOS2020 catalog and using a membership-probability approach to estimate group quiescent fractions. We compare these quiescent fractions to the expected cold or hot accretion state of each halo and find evidence for a correlation: quiescent fractions reach about 50 percent in groups in the hot-accretion regime and are consistent with zero in groups in the cold-accretion regime. In mature hot-accreting groups, massive quiescent galaxies are preferentially found in the inner regions ($R<0.5R_{\rm vir}$), with a 4.4-sigma excess relative to the outskirts. Most groups lack a clearly established brightest group galaxy and instead show small stellar-mass gaps, typically $M_{*,1}/M_{*,2}<3$, indicating that they remain in an active assembly phase rather than being dynamically evolved systems. Consistently, the stellar-mass excess of the dominant galaxy, measured relative to the SHMR expectation, does not predict the group quiescent fraction. Taken together, our results support a picture in which the cold-to-hot transition in gas accretion contributes to the onset of quiescence, possibly through inside-out starvation associated with filament disruption in shock-heated intra-group gas, and suggest that environment plays a greater role than internal processes in shaping the quiescent galaxy population in these structures.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.06162.title: Vacuum polarization and cyclotron resonance effects on radiative transfer and plasma deceleration in subcritical X-ray pulsars
arxiv.org/abs/2605.06162.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.06162v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate the spectrum and polarization of radiation emerging from a subcritical X-ray pulsar using self-consistent radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of an accretion channel in a strong magnetic field. The polarized radiative transfer in the channel above the hot spot is simulated for the two normal modes, taking into account resonant Compton scattering in a strongly magnetized plasma and the effects of vacuum polarization. We show that the deceleration of the accreting matter in the subcritical regime is mainly governed by resonant scattering. Our simulations provide the velocity profiles of the plasma flow and demonstrate that vacuum polarization dominates over plasma birefringence, enhancing both the cyclotron spectral feature and the radiative deceleration of the plasma. We also find that the energy of the cyclotron feature increases with accretion luminosity, indicating a positive correlation consistent with previous observational results and theoretical interpretation.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.02719.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
arxiv.org/abs/2606.02719.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.02719v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 11 (3) percent (four and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.05166.title: Compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck low-$\ell$ data
arxiv.org/abs/2606.05166.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.05166v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data, constructed from the SRoll2 likelihood which provides the tightest constraint on the reionization optical depth $\tau$ to date. The non-Gaussian form of CMB low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods makes them incompatible with Fisher matrix analyses that require an analytic Gaussian $\chi^2$, such as the Fisher-bias formalism and Fisher forecasts. We show that the $\chi^2$ of an offset log-normal likelihood takes a Gaussian form in the log-transformed power spectrum amplitudes, and can therefore serve as a proxy for the true Gaussian likelihood of this variable in Fisher matrix analyses, without any explicit change of variables. Building on this, we compress the SRoll2 likelihood into a small number of piecewise offset log-normal functions and validate it against the full SRoll2 likelihood via MCMC combined with Planck and ACT DR6 data, finding excellent agreement across all $\Lambda$CDM parameters and in extended cosmological models. We further demonstrate that Fisher matrix uncertainty estimates from our compressed likelihood agree well with the full MCMC posteriors. We release our compressed likelihood planck-gaussian-lowl, a lightweight Python package incorporating the compressed low-$\ell$ TT likelihood from previous work, allowing a straightforward incorporation of the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ data into any Gaussian-likelihood-based analysis. The package is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}{github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.11300.title: Calibration of CMB Polarisation Using Cross-Experiment Correlations
arxiv.org/abs/2606.11300.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.11300v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Parity-violating physics in the Universe can generate correlations between the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) $E$- and $B$-modes, but detecting such signals requires extremely accurate calibration of instruments. We describe a data-driven method to calibrate the relative polarisation angle between CMB experiments using cross-correlations of observations over a common sky region. Unlike standard self-calibration approaches, this method does not assume vanishing isotropic cosmic birefringence or primordial $EB$ correlations when estimating the relative misalignment angle, and therefore preserves sensitivity to parity-violating physics. As a proof of concept, we forecast the performance of this method using the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) as a calibrated reference. If they can be calibrated to an uncertainty of $0.08^\circ$, as anticipated from the SO wire grid calibration system, we show that the SO Large Aperture Telescope and Planck could be calibrated to uncertainties of $0.10^\circ$ and $0.17^\circ$, respectively, at $\sim 145$ GHz. This approach relies on the availability of at least one well-calibrated instrument, and provides a complementary path to improving polarisation calibration across experiments, enabling more robust searches for parity-violating physics in the CMB, such as cosmic birefringence.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.18908.title: Impact of lensing magnification on the power spectrum turnover
arxiv.org/abs/2606.18908.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.18908v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The turnover scale $k_0$ of the matter power spectrum -- and consequently of the standard galaxy power spectrum monopole -- encodes a fundamental signature of matter-radiation equality and constitutes an important standard ruler independent of baryon acoustic oscillations. In principle, we can detect the turnover at multiple redshifts and amplify the signal by stacking redshift bins. However, in spectroscopic surveys reaching high redshifts, such as the Euclid H$\alpha$ survey and the proposed MegaMapper Lyman-break galaxy survey, the monopole of the observed galaxy power spectrum receives a scale-dependent correction from lensing magnification. This can modify the signal shape and shift the turnover scale, undermining its use as a standard ruler. Using mock surveys similar to Euclid and MegaMapper, we forecast this shift and the consequent bias in the turnover scale that is recovered from the mock data. The shift in the turnover scale grows with redshift, leading to a maximum bias of $\sim 0.4\sigma$ (Euclid-like) and $\sim 3.6\sigma$ (MegaMapper-like). To avoid a bias $>1\sigma$, the maximum redshift for a MegaMapper-like survey is $z\approx 2.9$. Data in the remaining range $2.9\lesssim z\le 5$ does not directly provide a reliable recovery of the intrinsic turnover. In fact, we find that the turnover vanishes in a MegaMapper-like survey for $z\gtrsim 3.7$. Our results show that the lensing correction to the monopole should be included and carefully modelled when surveys are used to measure the cosmological turnover at high redshifts.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.21606.title: Carruthers Data Processing Pipeline: Instrument Effect Correction
arxiv.org/abs/2606.21606.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.21606v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The Carruthers Geocorona Observatory -- launched in September 2025 -- is NASA's first mission devoted to investigating the fundamental nature of Earth's exosphere from its distant vantage in halo orbit around the Earth-Sun L1 Lagrange point. Its primary payload, the GeoCoronal Imager, consists of two coaligned photometric imagers that measure ultraviolet Lyman-alpha emission radiance from exospheric hydrogen simultaneously at wide- and narrow- fields of view. The imagers use MicroChannel Plate intensified Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor detectors, which are known to add various artifacts to the final image telemetered from the spacecraft, hereby known as instrument effects. This paper details the algorithms used to retrieve and remove instrument effects from raw telemetry on-orbit, including detector voltage bias, thermal dark current, particle radiation, flat-field, and distortion. Finally, the science data processing pipeline from raw telemetry to instrument-effect corrected images is detailed. Algorithm performance is measured via a synthetic numerical image generator or validated on pre-launch experiments.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.00433.title: Heavy-element dust as an explanation for the late-time kilonova spectra
arxiv.org/abs/2607.00433.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.00433v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Neutron star mergers are a leading site of r-process, producing radioactively powered optical and infrared transients known as kilonovae. Observations of the kilonovae AT2017gfo, associated with the gravitational-wave event GW170817, and AT2023vfi, associated with GRB 230307A, have enabled measurements of the mass of ejected r-process material and identification of heavy elements in the ejecta. However, late-time observations reveal strong infrared emission with temperature below 1000 K, which is difficult to explain by atomic absorption and emission processes alone. In this paper, we propose that kilonova ejecta provide conditions favorable for the formation of dust grains composed of refractory r-process elements including Zr, W, and Os. Assuming a simplified, empirically derived single power-law temperature evolution and using W reaction rate coefficients as a proxy, our kinetic dust formation calculations indicate that dust could form efficiently, particularly in slow ejecta. This stands in contrast to a previous study that relied on a classical nucleation framework. By performing radiative transfer simulations that incorporate dust formation, we demonstrate that, if formed, r-process dust could naturally explain the observed late-time infrared emission, although refining ejecta parameters and geometry will be necessary to match specific observational cases. The formation and abundance of r-process dust are highly sensitive to ejecta mass, composition, and expansion velocity. Infrared emission from r-process dust may therefore potentially serve a new probe of heavy-element production in neutron star mergers.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.13019.title: Gamma-Ray Modes in a Transitional Pulsar
arxiv.org/abs/2607.13019.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.13019v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Transitional millisecond pulsars (tMSPs) exhibit a unique subluminous disk state, at the crossroads between accretion and rotation power, where they switch between two distinct X-ray modes. We present the discovery of gamma-ray modes in PSR J1023+0038, the first confirmed tMSP, from stacking Fermi-LAT data during the modes (which we identify using simultaneous X-ray observations). Surprisingly, we find that gamma rays and X-rays are anticorrelated during this mode switching: the gamma-ray flux is higher in the X-ray low mode, and vice versa. This contradicts the state-of-the-art model, which predicts bright gamma rays only in the X-ray high mode, from the interaction between the pulsar wind and surrounding disk via synchrotron and inverse Compton processes. Because the pulsar wind is likely absent in the gamma-ray high (X-ray low) mode, which is also brighter in the radio band, we suggest that jet emission may be dominant in GeV gamma rays. We also discuss an alternative interpretation where the gamma-ray high mode is powered by self-synchrotron Compton emission in the propeller state.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.24910.title: Cosmological evolution with decaying dark matter: an integral-equation approach
arxiv.org/abs/2607.24910.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.24910v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present CLASSIER-DDM, an extension of the Boltzmann solver CLASSIER that implements the decaying dark matter (DDM) model via its integral-equation approach. The code handles generic two-body decays of a dark matter particle into two lighter decay products with arbitrary masses, naturally encompassing both massless (dark radiation) and massive (warm) decay products, with their perturbations evaluated via integral equations solved iteratively. We describe the numerical implementation in detail, including the background evolution, the iterative perturbation evolution, and a small-scale analytic approximation. A modest number of iterations is sufficient to achieve sub-$0.1\%$ convergence in the matter power spectrum and the CMB lensing power spectrum across the observationally relevant parameter space. We find that a hundred momentum bins for the decay product perturbations are sufficient to achieve $\mathcal{O}(0.1\%)$ accuracy in the matter power spectrum today up to $k \sim 3\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. The code achieves $\mathcal{O}(1\,{\rm min})$ runtimes per evaluation, requiring neither a Boltzmann hierarchy nor any fluid approximation, making parameter estimation with the DDM model numerically tractable. We also discuss the impact of DDM on cosmological observables, focusing on the case of two massive decay products. This work further establishes the integral-equation approach as a versatile and efficient framework for modeling non-cold relics in cosmological perturbation theory.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.28530.title: Is the Quiet-Sun Heating Requirement Observationally Established?
arxiv.org/abs/2607.28530.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.28530v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: How much energy does the quiet corona require? Its radiation shows that energy must be supplied. Electrons also carry heat into or out of it. We ask whether temperature observations justify the heat-flow estimate used to judge a heating mechanism's energy supply. Two radio methods give temperatures near 0.62 and 1.5 million kelvin. A population with extra fast electrons can give both readings. Unresolved structure and delayed ion formation also leave Maxwellian explanations open. Neither temperature interpretation alone determines the heat flow. The tested local conduction formula diverges for the idealized fast-electron model with an unbroken tail. Applying X-ray limits to the model still leaves about 5--6% of the electrons holding 28--33% of its kinetic energy. The heat they carry depends on the balance between directions and on conditions along their paths. Source and collision calculations test whether the population could be sustained. The observations examined here do not establish whether the conductive estimate is accurate enough for the heating comparison. We cannot judge whether a mechanism supplies enough energy against a heat loss we have not established. Measuring, reliably calculating, or sufficiently bounding that loss would settle this part of the budget.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.01940.title: Environmental dependence of galaxy properties in the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey: Star formation, morphology, and AGN activity at z < 0.55
arxiv.org/abs/2608.01940.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.01940v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We examined the environmental dependence of galaxy properties using a parent sample of about 1.4 million BGS_BRIGHT galaxies from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey at $0.05 < z < 0.55$. Using the extended halo-based group catalogue, we measured how the specific star formation rate (sSFR), S\'{e}rsic index, and active galactic nucleus fraction depend on halo mass over $9\leq\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)<12$ and $12.5\leq\log(M_h/\mathrm{M}_\odot)<16$. The parent measurements describe the observed sample, and our main conclusions about the galaxy population are based on comparisons above the completeness limit derived for quiescent galaxies.
  Within the same stellar mass and redshift bins, the median sSFR is generally lower in clusters than in the field. At intermediate stellar masses and $z<0.25$, satellites show a lower median sSFR than centrals at fixed stellar and halo mass. The environmental dependence of the star formation reflects differences between centrals and satellites and the changing satellite fraction. The S\'{e}rsic index increases only weakly with halo mass at fixed stellar mass and redshift. Among galaxies in which all four diagnostic emission lines are detected, we find no strong environmental dependence of Seyfert or low-ionisation nuclear emission-line region fractions at fixed stellar mass. They are both marginally higher at most in clusters, with the largest but most uncertain differences at the highest stellar masses.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.03205.title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
arxiv.org/abs/2608.03205.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.03205v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3\,hr. Our observations span 0.65-233 GHz from 6-356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium ($n_e\propto R^{-k}$; $k= 1.5-2$). We detect significant variability in the low frequency ($\leq3$ GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of $1.2\times10^{16}\lesssim R_{\perp} \lesssim 5\times10^{17}$ cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle $\theta_j\gtrsim15$ deg, low Lorentz factor ($\Gamma\lesssim10$) jet, or a narrow $\theta_j\lesssim2$ deg highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs ($E_K\sim10^{51}$ erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs ($E_K\sim10^{50}$ erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.18207.title: The fraction of periodic SN Ib/c light curves
arxiv.org/abs/2608.18207.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.18207v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Periodic luminosity modulations have been recently identified for the stripped-envelope supernovae SN 2022jli and SN 2022esa, motivating a systematic search for a similar behavior in a larger sample. Such modulations may indicate the explosions arise in binary progenitor systems. We perform the first systematic search for periodic modulation in a sample of 34 Type Ib/c supernovae with high quality photometry from the Zwicky Transient Facility. We develop and apply a statistically rigorous pipeline for detecting periodic modulation in light curves. The pipeline successfully recovers the previously reported periodic undulations of SN 2022jli and SN 2022esa, and identifies SN 2020sgf as an additional promising periodic candidate. Injection-recovery simulations are used to quantify the survey sensitivity as a function of period and modulation amplitude. Comparing the observed detections with recent population synthesis models shows that, under the adopted assumptions, models predicting intrinsic periodic fractions of order ~20% are consistent with the observations. Given that this inference rests on only three dual-band detections out of 34 candidates, we regard this fraction as illustrative rather than a precise measurement. Our results suggest that periodically modulated SN 2022jli-like events may represent a non-negligible sub-population of stripped-envelope supernovae rather than being exceptionally rare events, while demonstrating a methodology suitable for future wide-field transient surveys.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.22231.title: The Cosmic Ultraviolet Background at the Galactic Poles
arxiv.org/abs/2608.22231.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.22231v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We have used archival \galex\ data to separate the cosmic ultraviolet background at the Galactic Poles into two components: the dust scattered light and an offset. We have modeled the dust-scattered light using a single-scattering model finding $1 \sigma$ limits of 0.54 -- 0.71 for the albedo ($a$) and 0.74 -- 0.83 for the phase function asymmetry factor ($g$) at 1530 \AA\ and 0.66 -- 0.73 for $a$ and 0.71 -- 0.77 for $g$ at 2360 \AA, that is, the grains are moderately reflective and highly forward-scattering.
  The offsets are 277 -- 284 \photu\ at 1530 \AA\ and 513 -- 520 \photu\ at 2360 \AA. After accounting for all known Galactic and extragalactic sources, we are left with an excess of $165 \pm 18$ \photu\ at 1530 \AA\ and $346 \pm 34$ at 2360 \AA. The offsets are constant over these regions with variances of 20 -- 30 \photu. Both the intensity and shape (NUV-to-FUV ratio) of this unexplained signal appear consistent with predictions based on emerging dark-matter candidates known as Axion Quark Nuggets (AQN).

arxiv.org/abs/2608.30698.title: Constraining Baryonic Feedback at $z\sim 1$ with the H$\alpha$ Luminosity Function
arxiv.org/abs/2608.30698.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.30698v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Baryonic feedback remains one of the primary uncertainties in galaxy formation models because of its impact on the interstellar medium (ISM) and star formation. We investigate its effect on the H$\alpha$ luminosity function (LF) using the Illustris and IllustrisTNG simulations. We incorporate direction- and metallicity-dependent dust attenuation, thermal sputtering and a physically motivated treatment of the propagation of Lyman-series photons. We model three sources of H$\alpha$ emission: star-forming H II regions, collisional excitation and recombination in the diffuse ISM, and AGN-induced photo-excitation of diffuse gas. The models are calibrated against observed H$\alpha$ LF at $z\sim1-1.5$ using a single free parameter relating the star formation rate to the H II-region H$\alpha$ luminosity. We find that, for $L_{\text{H}\alpha}\geq 10^{41}\ \rm{erg \ s^{-1}}$, emission from diffuse gas contributes $\sim 5\%-15\%$ of the total H$\alpha$ luminosity in both simulation sets. AGN photo-excitation produces only a modest enhancement of the bright end of the LF, although it dominates the H$\alpha$ emission of Illustris galaxies with $L_{\text{H}\alpha}\gtrsim \times10^{43}\ \rm{erg \ s^{-1}}$. The low-feedback IllustrisTNG simulations provide a good fit to the observed LF for all emission models considered, whereas the high-feedback Illustris predictions are difficult to reconcile with both the bright and faint end of the LF. This tension between H$\alpha$ LF and stacked kSZ measurements highlights the combined power of these probes for constraining the interplay between baryonic feedback, gas properties, and the physics governing emission-line galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.06150.title: Implementation of a five-wave approximate Riemann solver for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics in AthenaK
arxiv.org/abs/2609.06150.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.06150v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present an implementation of an HLLD approximate Riemann solver for the AthenaK astrophysics code with support for full general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics via a tetrad frame transformation. Our implementation uses an initial guess for the HLLD iterative solve which eliminates the need for an additional conserved-to-primitive inversion, which greatly accelerates performance without affecting accuracy. Additionally, by coupling the method with a first-order flux correction, we are able to use the method reliably even when the magnetization exceeds $10^4$, which we achieve in a SANE accretion disk. Our SANE disk shows that HLLD leads to a more strongly magnetized funnel and more accurate horizon fluxes when compared with HLLE. We further apply the new HLLD implementation to an equal-mass binary neutron star merger. For our long-lived remnant, HLLD enhances the magnetic shear stresses in the outer layers and leads to weaker differential rotation. However, due to weaker gravitational wave emissions in the post-merger phase, the remnant is consistently less compact while producing more dynamical ejecta and a more massive disk. The cost of this new solver is relatively modest thanks to the improved initial guess: our accretion disk tests are only ${\sim}10-25\%$ slower than HLLE, and for our binary neutron star runs with a microphysical equation of state, we find that HLLD is only ${\sim}3\%$ slower than HLLE across all runs.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.09063.title: The size and mass distribution of cold classical TNOs for $5<H<13$
arxiv.org/abs/2609.09063.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.09063v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The cold classical trans-Neptunian objects (CCs) are the only observable \textit{in situ} population of planetesimal remnants believed to have escaped collisional grinding. Recent JWST observations make it possible to fit the differential absolute magnitude distribution $dN/dH$ of the CCs from $5<13,$ and infer the differential mass distribution $dN/dM$ across $\ge5$ orders of magnitude in mass. We find $dN/dM$ well fit by a lognormal distribution, and equally well by a generalized $\Gamma$ distribution or a double power law. The maximum fraction of the total CC mass per log interval in $M$ is in bodies near 75~km diameter, or $\approx10^{-7.5}M_\oplus.$ Extrapolation of the fitted $dN/dH$ functions to $H_r>13$ is unwise, as the different analytic forms diverge. It remains unclear if $dN/dH$ turns over at faint $H.$
  The uncertainty in the total mass of the CC belt is dominated by uncertainty in the relation between $M$ and $H$. A calibration using CC binaries suggests a total CC mass of 1.7--2.7$\times10^{-3}\,M_\oplus.$ A trend toward lower density and/or higher albedo for smaller bodies may be present in the data, and would lower the estimated total CC mass.
  Qualitative comparison of the derived mass distribution to the results of numerical simulations of the streaming instability (SI) suggest the simulations produce $dN/dM$ distributions that are more sharply peaked, and steeper at the bright end, than the CCs. Such differences could be ascribed to inhomogeneous formation conditions in the classical belt that are not yet included in modeling. The variety and uncertainty of $dN/dM$ derived from state-of-the-art SI simulations currently preclude any definitive test of the SI hypothesis.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.30551.title: Breaking the AGB Color Degeneracy with Variability and H$_2$O: A Consistent Picture of AGB Chemistry, Dust, and the J-Region Across Environments
arxiv.org/abs/2609.30551.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.30551v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Resolved asymptotic giant branch (AGB) populations present many observational puzzles. We consider three often treated separately: photometric C/O classification boundaries must be redrawn empirically in new environments; hydrostatic model grids are too blue in bands sampling H2O absorption; and J-region (JAGB) luminosities can differ between fields of a single galaxy. Pulsation connects them into a coherent picture. Using SPHEREx spectroscopy of AGB stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) with JWST/NIRCam photometry and HST time-series of the SN Ia host M101, placed on a common scale by synthetic photometry, we investigate how AGB variability, surface chemistry, and circumstellar dust depend on environment. We develop an F182M index sensitive to 1.9$\mu$m H2O absorption that chemically classifies variable AGB stars and reveals oxygen-rich (O-rich) stars degenerate with carbon-rich (C-rich) stars in broadband colors. Because these features arise in extended atmospheric layers, hydrostatic grids struggle to reproduce them. Pulsation and circumstellar dust are asymmetrically linked: nearly all stars with substantial infrared excess are variable, while many variables show little dust. This supports mass loss initiated by pulsation and enhanced by dust formation. Variable O-rich AGB stars in M101 are up to ~0.7 mag redder than their LMC counterparts in dust-sensitive colors, consistent with more efficient silicate-dust production at higher metallicity, while C-rich populations depend less on environment. Color windows that select C-rich stars cleanly in the LMC are therefore 33-68% O-rich in the metal-rich M101. This challenges the J-region's universality as a standard candle while evading standard self-consistency checks. We recommend combining variability, or the infrared excess that implies it, with photometry of molecular features to improve AGB classification at 0.75-5.0$\mu$m.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12398.title: ACORN I. Massive Black Hole Seeding and Tidal Disruption Events from Star Clusters in Cosmological Simulations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12398.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12398v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: JWST has revealed massive star clusters at $z\gtrsim 6$, which provide promising environments for massive black hole (MBH) seed formation. We introduce a new MBH seeding model for cosmological simulations, physically motivated by runaway collisions in star clusters. Subgrid star clusters are generated according to the local ISM and evolved through stellar evolution and two-body relaxation. The masses of MBH seeds formed through runaway collisions are determined by the properties of their host clusters, including the effects of metallicity-dependent stellar winds. We further follow tidal disruption events (TDEs) with the evolving clusters, which can be enhanced in MBH binaries, and account for gravitational-wave (GW) recoil following MBH mergers. We implement this model in a constrained simulation of a 5$\sigma$ overdense region, where seeds of $10^{3}-10^{5.6}\,M_\odot$ form in clusters with $10^{4}\leq m_{\rm SC}\leq 10^{8}\,M_\odot$. Because both the seed abundance and mass are directly connected to the local environment, we have a more physical $M_{\rm BH}\!-\!M_{\rm galaxy}$ scaling for low-mass galaxies ($M_{\rm galaxy}\sim10^{6-9}\,M_\odot$), a regime poorly described by previous seeding models. Multiple MBHs are naturally allowed to form in-situ within individual halos, producing a spatially clustered population. This increases the MBH merger rate by $\sim100$ relative to other seeding models, significantly enhancing the expected LISA event rate. TDEs can dominate the growth of $10^{3-4}\,M_\odot$ MBHs and produce luminous flares of $L_{\rm peak}\sim 10^{42-43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, increasing the observability of low-mass seeds. This seeding prescription accelerates early MBH growth at $z\gtrsim 8$, while subsequent self-regulated gas accretion drives the central MBH toward similar masses $\sim10^{9}\, M_\odot$ by $z=6$ across different seeding models.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.28443.title: Tight asteroseismic upper limits on hot subdwarf magnetism
arxiv.org/abs/2610.28443.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.28443v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The apparent absence of magnetism in subdwarf B stars (sdBs) has emerged as an outstanding observational puzzle, especially in light of their likely origin in binary interactions. Gravity-mode pulsations in some sdBs offer a unique opportunity to extend recent successes in asteroseismic magnetic field detection in red giants. In the presence of strong magnetic fields, gravity modes are expected to be significantly damped, suppressing their observed amplitudes. We place stringent upper limits on magnetic fields in 30 hot subdwarfs by using the observation of low-frequency dipole and quadrupole modes to rule out magnetic suppression. Even under conservative assumptions, our upper limits constrain near-surface magnetic fields to below a kilogauss in roughly half of our sample, with the strongest individual constraint reaching down to $\sim20\,\mathrm{G}$. These upper limits reinforce the apparent dearth of magnetic fields in hot subdwarfs and demonstrate asteroseismology as a powerful new probe of magnetism in these stars.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.30286.title: Nuclear Millimeter Continuum Emission in Radio-Quiet Active Galactic Nuclei: an ALMA Spectral and Variability Study
arxiv.org/abs/2610.30286.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.30286v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Unresolved millimeter (mm) emission is observed in radio-quiet (RQ) Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), but its physical origin remains debated. Self-absorbed synchrotron emission from the compact X-ray corona is one of the leading candidates. Previous support for this coronal synchrotron origin has mainly been based on variability and spectral indices in a few RQ AGN, with a lack of (quasi-)simultaneous broadband data for larger samples. We present Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) observations of nine nearby ($z \sim 0.008-0.064$) RQ AGN, obtained quasi-simultaneously at 100, 145, and 233 GHz. Based on power-law fits to the spectral energy distributions, we measure millimeter spectral indices ranging from $-0.05^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ to $0.88^{+0.12}_{-0.11}$. Furthermore, across two 100 GHz observing epochs per source, separated by $4-11$ days, we detect flux density variability of $30-56$% (>$3\sigma$ significance level) in three out of nine sources. Spectral slopes alone are insufficient to constrain the origin of the millimeter emission; however, the observed short-timescale variability and inferred brightness temperature values are consistent with a non-thermal emission mechanism arising from a compact emitting region with a size of $R_{\rm mm}< 10^3 - 10^4 R_{\rm g}$, such as the corona or a compact jet. Furthermore, we find a clear correlation between the 100/233 GHz and X-ray flux in our sample, and establish a new linear correlation between 145 GHz and X-ray emission.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.37596.title: A self-supervised machine learning approach to identify instrumental systematics in 21cm Cosmology
arxiv.org/abs/2610.37596.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.37596v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The primordial sound waves in the baryon-photon plasma are imprinted on the large-scale galaxy distribution as Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), serving as a cosmological standard ruler to constrain dark energy and the Hubble parameter. The upcoming 21cm intensity-mapping arrays are designed to map the 21cm emission across large volumes and measure the BAO scale. However, radio interferometers suffer from instrumental systematics that can hinder detection of the cosmological 21cm signal by leaking bright foregrounds into the signal-dominated modes. This work aims to demonstrate that a self-supervised model can predict the instrument systematic state (here, the amplitude of a spectral ripple in the beam width) in interferometric visibilities and potentially disentangle the instrument from the sky without a forward model. Based on the fact that an instrument stays the same as the sky rotates in a drift-scan observation, and that the same sky is observed under different instrument states, we train a convolutional autoencoder to compress the information in the simulated visibilities and separate this information into instrument-only and sky-only latent vectors. The result shows excellent prediction of the unknown instrument systematic for 15 held-out instrument states with $R^2 = 0.9975$ with a linear probe, against $R^2 = -3.55$ for a random-encoder baseline. The instrument-latent carries no detectable sky signal, as measured with a total-power sky proxy, for any held-out test data. The sky-latent vector and instrument-latent vector show partial separation but not complete disentanglement, identifying sky-latent purity as the primary open problem. The results show the ability of the model to recognize the systematic and show a promising path towards an ML-based foreground cleaning pipeline. Full instrument-sky disentanglement constitutes the natural next step.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.40008.title: Identifying narrow-band mutual coupling resonances in SKA-low stations using frequency-independent current basis functions
arxiv.org/abs/2610.40008.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.40008v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Mutual coupling between closely spaced elements in aperture arrays introduces narrow-band spectral features in the Embedded Element Patterns (EEPs), threatening measurements of the 21-cm power spectrum with instruments such as SKA-low. We detail a method to identify such features through the construction of frequency-independent current basis functions, utilising a singular value decomposition of frequency-dependent basis functions. We demonstrate the method on a three-element linear array and full pseudo-random station of SKA log-periodic antennas and examine the current power induced by mutual coupling. For the pseudo-random layout station we note many narrow-band resonance features, including strong resonances at 50.8~MHz and 83.6~MHz, where the coupled power on the passive antennas can approach or exceed that of the excited antenna. Simulated delay power spectra for the SKA-low core show that observing in frequency bands including resonance features causes large foreground leakage within the delay power spectra, obscuring the EoR window. For the pseudo-random layout station with SKALA4.0 we identify two significant frequency bands from 59.2--76.2~MHz and 84.2--103.3~MHz which are free of contamination from current resonances, preserving the EoR window in these frequency ranges.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.00329.title: Slowly rotating white dwarfs in f (R, T ) = R + 2{\lambda}T gravity: structure and stationary tidal response
arxiv.org/abs/2611.00329.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.00329v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We calculate the structure and stationary tidal response of cold carbon fluid white dwarfs in $f(R,T)=R+2\lambda T$ gravity through second order in uniform rotation. Equilibria are compared at fixed baryon number, with angular momentum also conserved during each aligned electric quadrupolar tidal perturbation. Negative coupling increases radii and dimensional tidal deformabilities over the common mass range. For the baryon sequence studied, background readjustment accounts for 95.8--97.5\% of the rotational enhancement at 40\% of each model's Kepler reference frequency. The explicit mixed rotational tidal contribution is positive and numerically resolved, but subdominant. At that spin, the enhancement relative to each coupling's static model decreases from 107.4\% in general relativity to 14.2\% at the most negative coupling, despite its larger absolute deformability. This reduction reflects less relative background expansion and a different Love-number variation.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.03131.title: Molecular gas in the disks and tails of ram pressure stripped Coma galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2611.03131.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.03131v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present new IRAM 30 m observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission in five Coma cluster galaxies undergoing ram pressure stripping. Molecular gas is detected in four galaxies, and CO emission is clearly detected in the stripped tails of three, extending up to $\sim50$ kpc from the stellar disks. The molecular gas masses in the tails range from a few $\times10^8\,M_\odot$ and account for up to 10-20% of the molecular gas remaining in the parent disks. Compared with field scaling relations, several galaxies exhibit elevated molecular-to-stellar gas ratios despite being H I deficient. This enhancement persists toward the lower-mass end of our sample, even in the massive Coma cluster environment, consistent with ram-pressure-induced compression of atomic gas and enhanced H I-to-H$_2$ conversion in the disks. At the same time, the total gas fractions of most galaxies remain close to those of field galaxies with similar stellar masses when the molecular gas in the tails is included, indicating that gas removal and phase transformation act simultaneously. We further investigate the relation between molecular and ionized gas by comparing CO and H$\alpha$ emission in the stripped regions. Although CO is preferentially detected in H$\alpha$-bright regions, the increased scatter compared with previous studies suggests the presence of both star-forming and diffuse CO components in the tails. Our results highlight the dual role of ram pressure stripping in dense environments: it efficiently removes gas from galaxies while also promoting molecular gas formation in both the disks and stripped material, thereby shaping short-term star formation in cluster galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.03846.title: SS 433 Eastern Jet Turbulence Revealed by Spatially-Resolved IXPE Data Analysis
arxiv.org/abs/2611.03846.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.03846v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The extended X-ray jet (EXJ) of SS 433/W50 shows hard X-ray and very-high-energy gamma-ray emission, indicating strong particle acceleration, likely sensitive to the EXJ magnetic field structure and turbulence. To study this field, we re-analyze the 2023 Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) observation of the eastern EXJ using the publicly available polarization fitting package LeakageLib. Compared with standard PCUBE and spectropolarimetric analyses, this approach improves the polarization constraints and enables spatially resolved polarization measurements. Dividing the EXJ into head, spine, and sheath regions with independent polarization properties, we find significant (>3 sigma) improvement over a single-zone model. The sheath exhibits lower polarization than the head and spine, while the electric vector position angles are consistent across all regions, indicating magnetic fields aligned with the jet axis. The measurements imply enhanced magnetic turbulence at the jet boundary, potentially driven by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.11075.title: Season by season causal analysis of the continuum and velocity-resolved H$\beta$ emission of NGC 5548
arxiv.org/abs/2611.11075.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.11075v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate possible causal influences in five historical seasons (1989-1993) of NGC 5548 using a version of the Synergistic-Unique-Redundant Decomposition (SURD) method adapted for this analysis, an information-theoretic causal discovery method for time series. Two four-variable sets contain the blue wing (B), core (C) and red wing (R) of H-beta together with either total H-beta (H) or the 5100 Angstrom continuum (F). We examine 7200 decompositions with common and unequal lags, two or three seasonal flux states, and base delays of 1-30 d. We rank the individual named components within each information family, reporting their amplitudes and simultaneous leakage. In 1989, unique continuum information about the core reaches 0.799 and 0.387 of target entropy for two and three states, with leakage 0.047 and 0.276. In 1992, the red-wing history supplies unique information about the future blue wing in both variable sets and both state counts, with peak target-entropy fractions 0.106-0.166. Distinct joint influences also emerge: for the 1991 core, the two-state S(F,B) and S(F,R) components contribute 0.187 and 0.125 at 20 d with leakage 0.087, although the unique continuum term vanishes. Strong core-wing redundancy identifies candidate inputs for simpler predictive models. Large late-lag leakage, reaching approximately 0.97 in the total set, identifies targets for additional driver measurements and richer temporal histories. The resulting seasonal map of individual, shared and joint influences complements the response delays and velocity structure measured by reverberation mapping, and provides specific causal hypotheses for the evolving broad-line region.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.12543.title: Kinematic Signatures of Stellar Flybys in Protoplanetary Discs
arxiv.org/abs/2611.12543.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.12543v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent high-resolution molecular line observations of protoplanetary discs have revealed large-scale non-Keplerian features in the gas kinematics of several systems, which can be interpreted as signatures of warps in the disc. Warps can arise from a range of physical mechanisms, and it remains unclear whether the observed kinematic residuals can be uniquely attributed to warping, or to different competing effects. Stellar flybys are one such mechanism capable of both warping a disc and directly perturbing its kinematics. Using 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations, we study the evolution of protoplanetary discs perturbed by inclined and coplanar stellar flybys, focusing on timescales of several thousand years after periastron rather than the immediate aftermath of the encounter. We find that inclined stellar flybys initially induce warping and twisting in the disc, but that this geometric perturbation is damped on a timescale set by the disc viscosity. Despite this geometric damping, synthetic ALMA observations of the CO kinematics show that complex non-Keplerian spiral features persist in the velocity residuals long after the warped morphology has relaxed, including in coplanar encounters where no warp is ever induced. Fitting these residuals with a simple warped-disc model, the degree of warping in the disc is systematically overestimated. We therefore conclude that kinematic residuals alone are insufficient to establish that a disc is warped, as flybys induce kinematic complexity independently of warps. We further show that scattered light observations provide an independent diagnostic, showing spiral arms and lateral asymmetries.

arxiv.org/abs/2611.12595.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
arxiv.org/abs/2611.12595.excerpt:
arXiv:2611.12595v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN).
